metadata.title: Claude Doesn't Design a New Zoom Chat App — It Assembles Into Yours.
metadata.topic: BUILD ZOOM TEAM CHAT APP · ANTHROPIC SKILL
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: what does build-zoom-team-chat-app actually add to Claude? Take the file apart and show the mechanism — a folder holding one SKILL.md, a fixed six-item coverage list, a linear read-then-execute pipeline — then name the design choice: a bounded, reproducible surface plugged into an existing chat client, at the expense of ever designing a new one.

beats.narration_text: Read 'build-zoom-team-chat-app' and it sounds like Claude designs a new Zoom client from scratch. It doesn't — it assembles one. One instruction file, one bounded list of parts, plugged into the chat that's already there.

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: Here's what the machinery actually is: a folder — build-zoom-team-chat-app — with one SKILL.md inside. Plain-English instructions Claude reads before it does anything. That file names six things, and only six: user-scoped messaging integrations, chatbot experiences, rich cards, buttons, slash commands, chat webhooks. Claude reads the file; then it does what the file says. No taste is added by the folder — the folder adds a specification.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon opening to reveal SKILL.md, references/, scripts/; SKILL.md highlighted; caption lists the six chat surfaces

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens on cream to reveal three items: SKILL.md (highlighted in crimson), a references/ folder, a scripts/ folder. A caption below reads 'Claude reads it, then follows it.' with a second line listing the six covered chat surfaces.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline is boring on purpose. Read the file. Walk each step in the order written. Return the result. No branching, no shortcuts — unless the file itself tells it to branch. They optimized for reproducibility: same document in, same run out. That's the payoff, and that's the ceiling.

production_viz.mechanic: Three cards left to right joined by arrows: 'Read SKILL.md', 'Execute steps in order', 'Return result'. Linear, no branch points drawn.

beats.act: 3 constraint — one chat lane, six pieces
beats.narration_text: The skill only switches on after some other decision has already narrowed you to Zoom Team Chat. From there the coverage is finite and written down: user-scoped messaging integrations, chatbot experiences, rich cards, buttons, slash commands, chat webhooks. Six items — and every one of them assumes the client already exists. Nothing on the list is 'design a new Zoom client.' The design choice worth naming: bounded surface at the expense of ambition. Every piece plugs into the app; none of them replaces it.

shot.new_visual_element: Six coverage rows filling in with checkmarks; a boundary line beneath, faint field beyond captioned 'nothing outside this list'

production_viz.label: One chat lane, six pieces
production_viz.mechanic: Six rows fill in one at a time with a checkmark, two columns of three: 'Messaging integrations', 'Chatbot experiences', 'Rich cards', 'Buttons', 'Slash commands', 'Chat webhooks'. A dashed boundary line beneath the grid, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'nothing outside this list'.

beats.narration_text: build-zoom-team-chat-app doesn't hand Claude a blank page. It hands Claude one instruction file — and Claude assembles exactly what that file lists: bots, cards, buttons, slash commands, into the Zoom chat you already have. Design lives inside the file; the app itself is not up for redesign.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Ask it: I want to add a bot to Zoom Team Chat that posts a rich card with buttons when someone runs a slash command. Walk me through the pieces I'd need — the message payload, the card layout, and the webhook — before writing any code. Then have the model draw the wire between the three so I can see which piece fires when. Go deeper: ask which of the six things build-zoom-team-chat-app covers your app would actually need, which it wouldn't, and why — that's the seam between the checklist and your design.
